# 1. Why this audit exists

Fixture `C-05` got past the Stage 4.2F-B0.9 suite. A gate selected its population by a mutable property and then checked that property — so when the mutation made a record leave the population, the gate saw a smaller, still-correct population and passed. **A filter cannot observe its own departures.**

Every gate whose population is selected by a mutable property now carries three assertions rather than one: the property check, a named-membership assertion, and a population-count delta.

# 3. Documented exclusions

Naming members is only meaningful for a population whose membership is itself a governed fact. For open-ended populations a named list would have to be edited on every unrelated change, which trains the reader to ignore it. These five are excluded on purpose, each with the delta guard that covers it instead.

| ID | Selector | Used by | Why excluded | Delta guard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EXC-01 | every substantive string in the record set | FORBIDDEN_LABELS_ABSENT_FROM_EVERY_RECORD, CAIR_NOT_NAMED_INSTRUCTIONAL_DESIGNER, FINAL_CONTENT_IS_NOT_MARKED_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED | Population size is in the thousands and changes with any prose edit. The gate asserts an empty result over everything, which is the strongest form already — nothing can leave the population without leaving the model entirely. | the gate fails if the population reaches zero (NO_VACUOUS_GATES) |
| EXC-02 | every file in docs/pl06/t04/ | NO_T04_PPTX_ON_DISK | Directory contents legitimately grow every stage. Naming the members would require editing this list on every unrelated artifact addition, which trains the reader to ignore it. | the assertion is an empty result over all files, not over a subset |
| EXC-03 | every gate record emitted by this suite | EVERY_GATE_IS_TYPED, NO_DUPLICATE_GATE_IDS, NO_VACUOUS_GATES, EVERY_GATE_NAMES_ITS_SOURCE_ARTIFACT, EVERY_GATE_DECLARES_A_POPULATION | Self-referential and open by design — the suite grows. Membership is the whole suite, so nothing can leave it without being deleted, which the count catches. | ACTIVE_GATE_COUNT is reported and compared stage to stage |
| EXC-04 | every controlled source row referenced by the sequence or the quiz | EVERY_SOURCE_ROW_RESOLVES, EVERY_QUIZ_SOURCE_ROW_RESOLVES | The row set is large and is governed by the extraction stage's own suite, not this one. Duplicating 100 row IDs here would create a second source of truth. | SOURCE_BINDINGS_NOT_REMOVED_FROM_THE_MODEL asserts the prior row set is still fully covered — a genuine delta assertion |
| EXC-05 | every emitted artifact scanned for stale facts | NO_EMITTED_ARTIFACT_ASSERTS_A_STALE_FACT_AS_CURRENT | Artifact list grows per stage; membership is asserted separately by EVERY_DECLARED_ARTIFACT_WAS_EMITTED and TWENTY_FOUR_ARTIFACTS_DECLARED. | STALE_FACT_SCAN_ACTUALLY_MATCHED_SOMETHING prevents the scan going vacuously green |

# 4. XML element identity

Substring matching on OOXML is wrong in a way that reads as right. `<w:insideH>` starts with `<w:ins`; `<w:tcPr>` starts with `<w:t`. The first of those nearly produced a false claim that the authority document contained twelve tracked insertions. Element checks now match namespace plus local name exactly.

| Case | Kind | What it proves | Exact match | Naive substring | Naive would have been wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| XML-01 | CONFUSION | <w:insideH> is not <w:ins> | 0 | 1 | yes |
| XML-02 | CONFUSION | <w:insideV> is not <w:ins> | 0 | 1 | yes |
| XML-03 | CONFUSION | <w:tcPr> is not <w:t> | 0 | 4 | yes |
| XML-04 | POSITIVE_CONTROL | a real <w:ins> is still found | 1 | 1 | n/a — positive control |
| XML-05 | CONFUSION | a real <w:t> is still found alongside <w:tcPr> | 1 | 5 | yes |
| XML-06 | CONFUSION | <w:delText> is not <w:del> | 0 | 1 | yes |

`XML-04` is a positive control: it exists so the helper cannot pass by returning zero for everything.
